source.text: Καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἦλθαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ὅτι μετὰ γυναικὸς ἐλάλει· οὐδεὶς μέντοι εἶπεν· Τί ζητεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: And upon this came the disciples of him, and they were marveling that with a woman he was speaking; no one however said, "What do you seek?"

en.L: And at this [moment] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came, and they were marveling that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} seeking?"
en.B: At that moment {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples arrived, and they were astonished that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking with a woman. Yet none of them said, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} looking for?"
en.R: Right then Jesus's disciples came back. They were amazed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was talking with a woman. But none of them asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want from her?"

es.L: Y en esto llegaron sus discípulos, y se maravillaban de que hablara con una mujer; sin embargo, nadie dijo: «¿Qué buscas?»
es.B: En ese momento llegaron sus discípulos, y se quedaron asombrados de que estuviera hablando con una mujer. Pero ninguno le dijo: «¿Qué buscas?»
es.R: Justo entonces volvieron los discípulos de Jesús. Se sorprendieron de que hablara con una mujer. Pero ninguno le preguntó: «¿Qué quieres de ella?»

sw.L: Na wakati huo wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakaja, nao wakastaajabu kwamba alikuwa akizungumza na mwanamke; lakini hakuna aliyesema, "Unatafuta nini?"
sw.B: Wakati huo huo wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walifika, wakashangaa kwamba alikuwa akizungumza na mwanamke. Hata hivyo hakuna aliyemwuliza, "Unatafuta nini?"
sw.R: Wakati huo huo wanafunzi wa Yesu walirudi. Walishangaa kwamba alikuwa akizungumza na mwanamke. Lakini hakuna aliyemwuliza, "Unataka nini kwake?"

decisions.choice: at this: just as Jesus said "I am he" (4:26)
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the moment. The disciples, who had gone into the town to buy food (4:8), come back at the very point where Jesus has told the woman who he is, and the conversation ends.

decisions.choice: they were surprised that a teacher was talking in public with a woman
alternatives: surprised only that she was a Samaritan
decisions.reason: John says "a woman", not "a Samaritan": the surprise is that a teacher was talking alone with a woman he did not know. Jewish teaching of the time was wary of this; the Mishnah, collected about AD 200, records the saying "do not talk much with a woman" (Avot 1:5). That she was also a Samaritan (4:9) made it stranger still. The imperfect verb pictures their surprise as lasting while they took in the scene.

decisions.choice: both questions are ones they might have put to Jesus, and did not
alternatives: the first question is to the woman (what do you want?), the second to Jesus
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular, and the second question, "why are you speaking with her?", is plainly to Jesus; joined by "or", the two are most naturally alternatives put to the same person. μέντοι ("yet") shows that respect for their teacher kept them quiet. "What are you seeking?" is the question Jesus himself asked the first disciples (1:38).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "you" when people speak to him, as here, even though the question is not spoken aloud. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: What are you looking for? (B); What do you want from her? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same everyday words as at 1:38, so the echo stays visible; Readable says plainly what the question would have meant here and supplies "from her", which the scene implies.

decisions.choice: ¿Qué buscas? (L, B); ¿Qué quieres de ella? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same words as at 1:38 ("¿Qué buscan?"), so the echo stays visible; Readable says plainly what the question would have meant here.

source.text: ἢ τί λαλεῖς μετ’ αὐτῆς;

records.literal_gloss: Or why do you speak with her?

en.L: or, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speaking with her?"
en.B: or, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speaking with her?"
en.R: or, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} talking with her?"

es.L: o: «¿Por qué hablas con ella?».
es.B: ni: «¿Por qué hablas con ella?».
es.R: ni: «¿Por qué estás hablando con ella?».

sw.L: au, "Mbona unazungumza naye?"
sw.B: au, "Kwa nini unazungumza naye?"
sw.R: au, "Kwa nini unazungumza naye?"

decisions.choice: a second question, its own sentence in the SBLGNT but still governed by "no one said"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the first question with a question mark and begins this one with "or", so the record starts in the middle of the reported speech. Both questions belong to what the disciples did not say; the renderings begin in lower case so that the two records read as one sentence.

decisions.choice: ni (B, R); o (L)
decisions.reason: After "ninguno le dijo", Spanish joins the second question with "ni"; Literal keeps the Greek "or".

source.text: ἀφῆκεν οὖν τὴν ὑδρίαν αὐτῆς ἡ γυνὴ καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις·

records.literal_gloss: Left then the water jar of her the woman and went away into the city and says to the people:

en.L: So the woman left her water jar and went away into the town, and she says to the {{gender:people|men}},
en.B: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town and said to the {{gender:people|men}},
en.R: The woman left her water jar there and hurried back to the town. She said to the {{gender:people|men}} there,

es.L: Dejó, pues, la mujer su cántaro, y se fue al pueblo, y dice a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}:
es.B: Entonces la mujer dejó su cántaro, volvió al pueblo y dijo a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}:
es.R: La mujer dejó allí su cántaro y volvió deprisa al pueblo. Allí dijo a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}:

sw.L: Basi yule mwanamke akauacha mtungi wake, akaenda zake mjini, naye anawaambia watu,
sw.B: Kisha yule mwanamke aliuacha mtungi wake, akarudi mjini, akawaambia watu,
sw.R: Yule mwanamke aliuacha mtungi wake hapo, akarudi mjini haraka. Akawaambia watu wa huko,

decisions.choice: she left the jar behind as she went off to the town
alternatives: a deliberate sign that she no longer cares for well water (4:13-15)
decisions.reason: She came to draw water (4:7), and now she leaves the jar at the well, perhaps in haste and meaning to come back. Some readers see a picture in it: she has found the living water Jesus spoke of (4:10-14). John does not say so, so every level simply reports it.

decisions.choice: the town: Sychar (4:5)
decisions.reason: The word is used of any walled or settled place, small or large. Here it is Sychar, the town near Jacob's well (4:5).

decisions.choice: the people of the town, men and women
alternatives: only the men, gathered in a public place
decisions.reason: The plural of this word is the ordinary term for people in general; it does not mark them as male. Those she speaks to are the townspeople who then come out (4:30) and of whom many believe (4:39-42).

decisions.choice: the {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive word is the default and the gender setting gives the traditional "men".

decisions.choice: said
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("she says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage.

decisions.choice: town
decisions.reason: Sychar was a small place (meaning decision m2); "city" would suggest something much larger.

decisions.choice: hurried back
decisions.reason: Readable shows the haste implied by her leaving the jar and going at once.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("llega", "le dice"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general (meaning decision m3): inclusive default, traditional one tap away.

decisions.choice: cántaro
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one used for the stone jars of 2:6, which Spanish calls "tinajas". Here it is the jar she carried to the well, which Spanish calls a "cántaro".

source.text: Δεῦτε ἴδετε ἄνθρωπον ὃς εἶπέ μοι πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησα· μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός;

records.literal_gloss: "Come, see a man who told me all things as many as I did; can it be that this one is the Christ?"

en.L: "Come, see a man who told me all the things that I did. Can it be that this [man] is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"
en.B: "Come and see a man who told me everything I have done. Could this possibly be the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"
en.R: "Come and see a man who told me all the things I have ever done! Might {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"

es.L: «{{plural_you:Vengan, vean|Venid, ved}} a un hombre que me dijo todo lo que he hecho. ¿Acaso será este el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».
es.B: «{{plural_you:Vengan a ver|Venid a ver}} a un hombre que me ha dicho todo lo que he hecho. ¿No será este el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».
es.R: «¡{{plural_you:Vengan a ver|Venid a ver}} a un hombre que me dijo todo lo que he hecho en mi vida! ¿Será {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».

sw.L: "Njooni, mwone mtu aliyeniambia mambo yote niliyoyafanya. Je, yawezekana huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.B: "Njooni mwone mtu aliyeniambia kila kitu nilichowahi kufanya. Inawezekana huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.R: "Njooni mwone mtu aliyeniambia mambo yote niliyowahi kufanya! Huenda {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"

decisions.choice: everything I have done: an overstatement that sums up her life
alternatives: a full list of her deeds
decisions.reason: Jesus had told her about her five husbands and the man she now lived with (4:16-18). That he knew this was enough to show he knew her whole life. Her words also echo what she said of the Messiah: "he will tell us all things" (4:25).

decisions.choice: a hesitant question that hopes but does not claim: could this be the Christ?
alternatives: a question expecting yes: is not this the Christ?
a question expecting no: this cannot be the Christ
decisions.reason: μήτι normally introduces a question that expects "no" (as in 4:33). Here, as in Matthew 12:23, it voices a guarded hope: she does not dare to assert it, but she raises it so that others will come and judge for themselves. The renderings keep the question tentative. Some older versions turned it into a confident "Is not this the Christ?", which the form does not support.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the title, the Anointed One she has just spoken of (4:25)
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title. The woman herself used the Hebrew word Messiah, which John translates (4:25). Samaritans accepted only the five books of Moses, and their hope rested on the promise of a prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15-18); later Samaritan writings speak of a coming restorer who would reveal the truth.

decisions.choice: Come, see: she invites others as Philip invited Nathanael
decisions.reason: The two plural commands repeat the pattern of 1:39 and 1:46, "come and see": the one who has met Jesus brings others to see for themselves. The woman becomes the first witness to Jesus in Samaria (4:39).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, so every level writes "the" outside the span, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: Could this possibly be ...? (B); Might he be ...? (R)
alternatives: He cannot be the Christ, can he?
decisions.reason: These keep the hesitation of the question (meaning decision m2) without turning it into a denial or a confession.

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso será ...? (L); ¿No será ...? (B); ¿Será él ...? (R)
decisions.reason: These keep the hesitation of the question (meaning decision m2): "¿No será...?" voices a guarded hope in everyday Spanish, without turning it into a denial or a confession.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, as at 1:20.

source.text: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: They went out from the city and were coming toward him.

en.L: They went out of the town and were coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The people went out of the town and began making their way to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: So the people left the town and started out toward Jesus.

es.L: Salieron del pueblo y venían hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: La gente salió del pueblo y se puso en camino hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Entonces la gente salió del pueblo y se fue hacia donde estaba Jesús.

sw.L: Wakatoka mjini, wakawa wanakuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Watu walitoka mjini, wakaanza kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Basi watu waliondoka mjini, wakaanza safari kumwendea Yesu.

decisions.choice: they set out, and were on their way while Jesus spoke with his disciples
decisions.reason: The first verb tells of the setting out, the second (an imperfect) of a journey still going on. John leaves them coming across the fields during 4:31-38 and brings them to Jesus at 4:40. The harvest Jesus speaks of is coming toward him as he speaks.

decisions.choice: no connecting word (SBLGNT)
alternatives: "so they went out" (many later manuscripts add a connecting word)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a word for "so" or "then", as the King James Version reflects. The sense is the same, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: The people (B, R); Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, the townspeople of 4:28; Readable also names Jesus.

decisions.choice: began making their way (B); started out toward (R)
decisions.reason: Shows that they were still on the way (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: La gente (B, R); Jesús (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable name the subject; Readable also names Jesus.

source.text: Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ῥαββί, φάγε.

records.literal_gloss: In the meantime were asking him the disciples saying, "Rabbi, eat."

en.L: In the meantime the disciples were urging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Rabbi, eat."
en.B: Meanwhile the disciples kept urging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, eat something."
en.R: While this was happening, the disciples kept saying to Jesus, "Rabbi, please eat something."

es.L: Mientras tanto, los discípulos le rogaban, diciendo: «Rabí, come».
es.B: Mientras tanto, los discípulos le insistían: «Rabí, come algo».
es.R: Mientras pasaba esto, los discípulos le decían a Jesús una y otra vez: «Rabí, por favor, come algo».

sw.L: Wakati huo wanafunzi walikuwa wakimsihi, wakisema, "Rabi, kula."
sw.B: Wakati huo huo wanafunzi waliendelea kumsihi, "Rabi, kula kitu."
sw.R: Mambo hayo yalipokuwa yakiendelea, wanafunzi waliendelea kumwambia Yesu, "Rabi, tafadhali kula kitu."

decisions.choice: were urging him: kept asking him to eat
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "ask", and it can mean a request as well as a question. Here what follows is a request, and the imperfect shows them pressing it more than once.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: the respectful title for a teacher
decisions.reason: The disciples use the title John explained at 1:38. They had gone to the town for food (4:8) and now offer it to him.

decisions.choice: Rabbi
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: John translates the word himself (1:38), so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: something (B, R); please (R)
decisions.reason: A bare "eat" sounds abrupt; the words give the friendly tone of the disciples' request.

decisions.choice: algo (B, R); por favor (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: a bare "come" sounds abrupt; the words give the friendly tone. "Rabí" at every level, as at 1:38.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε.

records.literal_gloss: But he said to them, "I food have to eat which you not know."

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "I have food to eat that you do not know."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "I have food to eat that you are not aware of."
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I have a kind of food that you do not know about."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Yo tengo una comida que comer que {{plural_you:ustedes no conocen|vosotros no conocéis}}».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Yo tengo para comer un alimento que {{plural_you:ustedes no conocen|vosotros no conocéis}}».
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Yo tengo una clase de comida que {{plural_you:ustedes no conocen|vosotros no conocéis}}».

sw.L: Lakini akawaambia, "Mimi nina chakula cha kula ambacho ninyi hamkijui."
sw.B: Lakini akawaambia, "Mimi nina chakula cha kula msichokijua ninyi."
sw.R: Lakini akasema, "Nina chakula cha aina ambayo ninyi hamkijui."

decisions.choice: emphatic I and you: I have food; you do not know it
decisions.reason: Both pronouns are written out, which Greek does for emphasis: what sustains Jesus is something the disciples know nothing of.

decisions.choice: food in a sense beyond the literal, explained in verse 34
alternatives: Jesus has been given a meal
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of food as he spoke of water with the woman (4:10-15) and of the temple with the authorities (2:19-21): his hearers take him literally, and he then explains. The disciples misunderstand (4:33) just as the woman did.

decisions.choice: you do not know: you have no knowledge of it
decisions.reason: The verb is "know". They do not know that such food exists, nor what it is.

decisions.choice: you are not aware of (B); you do not know about (R)
decisions.reason: "Know" with "food" as its object is unnatural here; these say what it means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: que ustedes no conocen
decisions.reason: English needs "not aware of", but Spanish "conocer" takes a thing as its object naturally, so every level keeps the verb (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Μή τις ἤνεγκεν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Were saying therefore the disciples to one another, "Not anyone brought him to eat?"

en.L: So the disciples were saying to one another, "No one brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [anything] to eat, did they?"
en.B: So the disciples said to one another, "Nobody has brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} food, have they?"
en.R: So the disciples asked each other, "Did someone bring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} food while we were gone?"

es.L: Decían, pues, los discípulos unos a otros: «¿Acaso alguien le trajo de comer?».
es.B: Entonces los discípulos se decían unos a otros: «¿Le habrá traído alguien de comer?».
es.R: Los discípulos se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Alguien le trajo comida mientras no estábamos?».

sw.L: Basi wanafunzi walikuwa wakiambiana, "Hakuna aliyemletea [kitu] cha kula, sivyo?"
sw.B: Basi wanafunzi wakaulizana, "Hakuna aliyemletea chakula, sivyo?"
sw.R: Basi wanafunzi wakaulizana, "Je, kuna mtu aliyemletea chakula tulipokuwa hatupo?"

decisions.choice: a puzzled question that expects no
decisions.reason: Μή at the head of the question expects the answer "no": they cannot think who would have fed him in Samaria (4:9), yet they can find no other explanation.

decisions.choice: they take his words about food literally
decisions.reason: Like the woman with the water (4:11), the disciples think of ordinary food. Their question prepares for Jesus's explanation in the next verse.

decisions.choice: Did someone bring him food while we were gone?
alternatives: No one brought him food, did they?
decisions.reason: Readable asks the question plainly and adds "while we were gone", which the story implies (4:8); the puzzled tone remains.

decisions.choice: ¿Alguien le trajo comida mientras no estábamos?
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable asks the question plainly and adds what the story implies (4:8).

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ποιήσω τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με καὶ τελειώσω αὐτοῦ τὸ ἔργον.

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Jesus, "My food is that I do the will of the one having sent me and complete his the work."

en.L: Jesus says to them, "My food is that I should do the will of the [one] who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and should complete {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "My food is doing the will of the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and bringing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work to completion."
en.R: Jesus said, "My food is to do what God wants. He sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food is to finish {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work."

es.L: Jesús les dice: «Mi comida es que haga la voluntad del que me envió y que lleve a cabo su obra».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «Mi comida es hacer la voluntad del que me envió y terminar su obra».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Mi comida es hacer lo que Dios quiere. Él me envió, y mi comida es terminar el trabajo que me dio».

sw.L: Yesu anawaambia, "Chakula {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} ni kwamba niyafanye mapenzi ya yule aliyenituma na kuikamilisha kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Chakula {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} ni kufanya mapenzi ya yule aliyenituma, na kuikamilisha kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."
sw.R: Yesu akasema, "Chakula {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} ni kufanya kile ambacho Mungu anataka. Yeye ndiye aliyenituma, na chakula {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} ni kuimaliza kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."

decisions.choice: what sustains Jesus is doing the Father's will
decisions.reason: Food gives life and strength; Jesus says his life is fed by obedience. The thought is like Deuteronomy 8:3, that people do not live by bread alone. Later he says, "I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of him who sent me" (6:38).

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus often describes God as "the one who sent me" (5:24, 30; 6:38-39; 7:16). It presents him as the Father's envoy, who speaks and acts for the one who sent him.

decisions.choice: complete: carry through to the end
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring something to its goal. Jesus uses it again in his prayer, "I have completed the work you gave me to do" (17:4), and from the cross he says "It is finished" (19:30), from the same root.

decisions.choice: doing ... bringing ... to completion
alternatives: that I should do ... and complete (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the purpose clause into a plain description of what his food is.

decisions.choice: what God wants. He sent me
alternatives: the will of the one who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom "the one who sent me" means (meaning decision m2), and splits the long phrase into short sentences.

decisions.choice: lo que Dios quiere. Él me envió
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names God (meaning decision m2) and splits the long phrase. "Él" begins a sentence and is written plain.

source.text: οὐχ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Ἔτι τετράμηνός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται;

records.literal_gloss: Not you say that, "Yet four months it is and the harvest comes"?

en.L: "Do you not say, 'It is still four months, and the harvest comes'?
en.B: "Do you not say, 'Four months more, and the harvest will be here'?
en.R: "You say, 'In four more months the harvest will come.'

es.L: «¿No {{plural_you:dicen ustedes|decís vosotros}}: “Todavía faltan cuatro meses, y llega la cosecha”?
es.B: «¿No {{plural_you:dicen ustedes|decís vosotros}}: “Faltan cuatro meses para la cosecha”?
es.R: «{{plural_you:Ustedes dicen|Vosotros decís}}: “Dentro de cuatro meses llegará la cosecha”.

sw.L: "Je, ninyi hamsemi, 'Bado miezi minne, na mavuno yanakuja'?
sw.B: "Je, hamsemi, 'Bado miezi minne, kisha mavuno yatafika'?
sw.R: "Ninyi mnasema, 'Baada ya miezi minne mavuno yatafika.'

decisions.choice: a common saying, or a remark on the season: either way, "the harvest is still far off"
alternatives: a saying about the time between sowing and harvest
a time note: the scene is four months before harvest, in winter
decisions.reason: The words have the shape of a saying, and "do you not say" points to something people often said; the gap between sowing and the grain harvest was about this long. But no such saying is known from elsewhere, and the words may be a plain remark about the time of year, which would place the scene in winter, some four months before the harvest in spring. Either way the point is the same: the disciples think the harvest is still to come, and Jesus says it is here now.

decisions.choice: emphatic you: you say this, but I tell you (next sentence)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, setting the disciples' saying against Jesus's own words that follow.

decisions.choice: You say
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes", so Readable states it plainly.

decisions.choice: Ustedes dicen
decisions.reason: As in English: the question expects "yes", so Readable states it plainly.

source.text: ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας ὅτι λευκαί εἰσιν πρὸς θερισμόν· ἤδη ὁ θερίζων μισθὸν λαμβάνει καὶ συνάγει καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων.

records.literal_gloss: Look, I say to you, lift up the eyes of you and see the fields, that white they are toward harvest. \v 36 Already the one reaping a wage receives and gathers fruit into life eternal, so that the one sowing together may rejoice and the one reaping.

en.L: Look, I say to you, lift up your eyes and see the fields, that they are white for harvest. \v 36 Already the one who reaps is receiving wages and gathering fruit for eternal life, so that the one who sows and the one who reaps may rejoice together.
en.B: Listen, I tell you: raise your eyes and look at the fields. They have turned white, ready for harvest. \v 36 Already the reaper is being paid and is gathering a crop for eternal life, so that the sower may rejoice along with the reaper.
en.R: But I tell you, look up and see the fields! The grain is ripe and ready to harvest. \v 36 Already the harvester is getting paid and is gathering a crop for eternal life. So the one who plants and the one who harvests can be glad together.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren, yo les digo: levanten los ojos y miren|Mirad, yo os digo: levantad los ojos y mirad}} los campos, que están blancos para la siega. \v 36 Ya el que siega recibe salario y recoge fruto para vida eterna, para que el que siembra y el que siega se alegren juntos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen lo que les digo: levanten la vista y miren|Escuchad lo que os digo: levantad la vista y mirad}} los campos. Ya están blancos, listos para la cosecha. \v 36 Ya el segador está recibiendo su paga y recoge una cosecha para vida eterna, para que el que siembra se alegre junto con el que cosecha.
es.R: Pero yo {{plural_you:les digo: ¡levanten la vista y miren|os digo: ¡levantad la vista y mirad}} los campos! El grano ya está maduro y listo para la cosecha. \v 36 Ya el que cosecha está recibiendo su paga y está recogiendo una cosecha para vida eterna. Así, el que siembra y el que cosecha pueden alegrarse juntos.

sw.L: Tazama, nawaambia, inueni macho yenu mkayaone mashamba, kwamba ni meupe kwa ajili ya mavuno. \v 36 Tayari mvunaji anapokea mshahara na kukusanya matunda kwa ajili ya uzima wa milele, ili mpandaji na mvunaji wafurahi pamoja.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, nawaambia: inueni macho mtazame mashamba. Yamekuwa meupe, tayari kwa mavuno. \v 36 Tayari mvunaji analipwa, na anakusanya mavuno kwa ajili ya uzima wa milele, ili mpandaji afurahi pamoja na mvunaji.
sw.R: Lakini nawaambia, angalieni juu mwone mashamba! Nafaka imeiva, iko tayari kuvunwa. \v 36 Tayari mvunaji analipwa, na anakusanya mavuno kwa ajili ya uzima wa milele. Kwa hiyo yule anayepanda na yule anayevuna wanaweza kufurahi pamoja.

decisions.choice: white: grain ripened and turned pale, ready to cut
decisions.reason: Ripe wheat and barley turn from green to pale gold. Jesus speaks of the fields, and at the same time of the Samaritans who are coming out of the town toward him (4:30): they are the harvest that is ready now.

decisions.choice: already begins the next sentence: already the reaper is being paid
alternatives: already ends the sentence before: white for harvest already
decisions.reason: The manuscripts have no punctuation, and the word can end the sentence before or begin this one. The SBLGNT punctuates it with what follows, and John often puts "already" at the head of a clause (4:51; 7:14). The other reading, "white already for harvest", is old and well known from the King James Version, so a footnote gives it. Verse 36 is printed from "Already", as the punctuation suggests, though in the verse division the word stands at the end of verse 35.

decisions.choice: the harvest of the last days: people gathered for eternal life
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of God's final gathering as a harvest (Isaiah 27:12; Joel 3:13), and Jesus uses the image for people gathered to God (Matthew 9:37-38). Here the wage is the joy of the work, and the crop is people brought to eternal life.

decisions.choice: sower and reaper rejoice together: harvest comes straight after sowing
alternatives: no echo; only the shared joy is meant
decisions.reason: Normally sowing and reaping are months apart (verse 35), and the sower may never see the crop. Here they rejoice at the same time. Amos 9:13 pictures the age to come in the same way: the one plowing will overtake the one reaping. The link to Amos is possible but not stated.

decisions.choice: eternal life
alternatives: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: The book-wide key term for John, kept at every level.

decisions.choice: white
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of pale ripe grain; Readable says "ripe" so that young readers do not imagine snow (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Listen (B); But (R)
decisions.reason: The word calls attention to what follows; the style guide keeps "behold" out of modern English.

decisions.choice: is being paid / is getting paid
decisions.reason: Plain words for a worker's pay.

decisions.choice: blancos (L, B); maduro (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of pale ripe grain; Readable says "maduro" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Escuchen (B); Pero (R)
decisions.reason: The word calls attention to what follows; Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

source.text: ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ ὁ λόγος ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὅτι Ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ σπείρων καὶ ἄλλος ὁ θερίζων·

records.literal_gloss: For in this the saying is true that, "Another is the one sowing and another the one reaping."

en.L: For in this the saying is true: 'One is the one who sows, and another the one who reaps.'
en.B: For here the saying proves true: 'The sower is one person, and the reaper another.'
en.R: People say, 'One person plants and someone else harvests.' And here that saying is true.

es.L: Porque en esto es verdadero el dicho: “Uno es el que siembra, y otro el que siega”.
es.B: Pues aquí se cumple el dicho: “Uno siembra y otro cosecha”.
es.R: Hay un dicho: “Uno siembra y otro cosecha”. Y aquí ese dicho es verdad.

sw.L: Kwa maana katika hili msemo huu ni wa kweli: 'Mmoja ndiye anayepanda, na mwingine ndiye anayevuna.'
sw.B: Kwa maana hapa msemo ule unathibitika kuwa kweli: 'Mpandaji ni mtu mmoja, na mvunaji ni mwingine.'
sw.R: Watu husema, 'Mtu mmoja hupanda na mwingine huvuna.' Na hapa msemo huo ni kweli.

decisions.choice: the saying is true: the proverb really fits this case
alternatives: the saying is merely accurate in general
decisions.reason: The adjective means true in the sense of genuine, holding good. "In this" points to the situation Jesus has just described.

decisions.choice: a saying that usually complained of unfairness
decisions.reason: The Old Testament uses the thought as a curse or a lament: one sows and another eats the crop (Deuteronomy 28:30; Job 31:8; Micah 6:15). Here the same fact becomes a reason for shared joy (verse 36): others did the sowing, and the disciples reap.

decisions.choice: the saying first, then that it is true
alternatives: For in this the saying is true: ...
decisions.reason: Readable gives the saying before saying that it fits, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: one person ... another / someone else
decisions.reason: The words refer to anyone who sows or reaps; plain words for a person need no gender setting.

decisions.choice: the saying first, then that it is true
decisions.reason: As in English: easier to follow. "Uno ... otro" is general and needs no gender setting.

source.text: ἐγὼ ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς θερίζειν ὃ οὐχ ὑμεῖς κεκοπιάκατε· ἄλλοι κεκοπιάκασιν, καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν κόπον αὐτῶν εἰσεληλύθατε.

records.literal_gloss: I sent you to reap what not you have toiled; others have toiled, and you into the toil of them have entered.

en.L: I sent you to reap what you have not toiled over; others have toiled, and you have entered into their toil."
en.B: I sent you to reap what you did not labor over. Others did the labor, and you have taken up where their work left off."
en.R: I sent you to harvest a crop that you did not work for. Other people did the hard work before you, and now you are gathering what they worked for."

es.L: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envié a segar lo que {{plural_you:ustedes no han trabajado|vosotros no habéis trabajado}}; otros han trabajado, y {{plural_you:ustedes han entrado|vosotros habéis entrado}} en el trabajo de ellos».
es.B: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envié a cosechar lo que {{plural_you:ustedes no trabajaron|vosotros no trabajasteis}}. Otros hicieron el trabajo duro, y {{plural_you:ustedes han continuado|vosotros habéis continuado}} donde ellos lo dejaron».
es.R: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envié a cosechar algo por lo que {{plural_you:ustedes no trabajaron|vosotros no trabajasteis}}. Otros hicieron antes el trabajo duro, y ahora {{plural_you:ustedes recogen|vosotros recogéis}} el fruto de su esfuerzo».

sw.L: Mimi niliwatuma mvune kile ambacho hamkukitaabikia; wengine walitaabika, nanyi mmeingia katika taabu yao."
sw.B: Niliwatuma mvune kile ambacho hamkukifanyia kazi. Wengine walifanya kazi hiyo, nanyi mmeendeleza pale kazi yao ilipoishia."
sw.R: Niliwatuma mvune mavuno ambayo hamkuyafanyia kazi. Watu wengine walifanya kazi ngumu kabla yenu, na sasa ninyi mnakusanya kile walichokifanyia kazi."

decisions.choice: I sent you: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The disciples have not yet been sent out in this Gospel (17:18; 20:21). The past tense may look back to their call to follow him, or speak of their mission as already settled. The Samaritans coming out to Jesus (4:30) are the first crop they share in; later the apostles would preach in Samaria (Acts 8:4-25). The evidence does not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: others: those who worked before the disciples, not named
alternatives: John the Baptist and the prophets before him
the woman who brought her townspeople
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say who the others are. Jesus himself has just done the work in Samaria, and the woman has brought the town to him; the prophets and John the Baptist had prepared the ground before. Every level keeps "others" without naming them.

decisions.choice: toil: hard, wearying labor
decisions.reason: The verb and noun speak of tiring work. The same verb describes Jesus at the well, "tired from the journey" (4:6): the toil others have done includes his own.

decisions.choice: toiled, toil (L); labor (B)
decisions.reason: Literal repeats one word three times as the Greek does; Balanced keeps the sense of hard labor.

decisions.choice: Other people ... before you
decisions.reason: Readable shows that their work came first; the masculine plural refers to anyone, so plain "people" needs no setting.

decisions.choice: trabajar, trabajo (L); el trabajo duro (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal repeats one word three times as the Greek does; Balanced and Readable keep the sense of hard, wearying labor (meaning decision m3).

source.text: Ἐκ δὲ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν Σαμαριτῶν διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς γυναικὸς μαρτυρούσης ὅτι Εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα.

records.literal_gloss: From now the city that many believed in him of the Samaritans because of the word of the woman testifying that, "He told me all things which I did."

en.L: And from that town many of the Samaritans believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the word of the woman who testified, "He told me all the things that I did."
en.B: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the woman's word, as she testified, "He told me everything I have done."
en.R: Many Samaritans from that town believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of what the woman said. She told them, "He told me all the things I have ever done."

es.L: Y de aquel pueblo muchos de los samaritanos creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por la palabra de la mujer que daba testimonio: «Me dijo todo lo que he hecho».
es.B: Muchos de los samaritanos de aquel pueblo creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por la palabra de la mujer, que daba testimonio: «Me ha dicho todo lo que he hecho».
es.R: Muchos samaritanos de aquel pueblo creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por lo que les dijo la mujer: «Me dijo todo lo que he hecho en mi vida».

sw.L: Na kutoka mji ule Wasamaria wengi walimwamini kwa sababu ya neno la yule mwanamke aliyeshuhudia, "Aliniambia mambo yote niliyoyafanya."
sw.B: Wasamaria wengi wa mji ule walimwamini kwa sababu ya neno la yule mwanamke, alipokuwa akishuhudia, "Aliniambia kila kitu nilichowahi kufanya."
sw.R: Wasamaria wengi wa mji ule walimwamini kwa sababu ya yale aliyosema yule mwanamke. Aliwaambia, "Aliniambia mambo yote niliyowahi kufanya."

decisions.choice: believed in him: put their trust in Jesus
decisions.reason: "Believe in" with a person is John's phrase for trusting the person (2:11). They came to trust Jesus because of what she said, the way the Gospel expects later readers to believe through others' testimony (17:20; 20:31).

decisions.choice: testified: she bore witness
decisions.reason: John uses this verb for John the Baptist's witness to Jesus (1:7, 15, 32-34). The woman becomes a witness in the same way.

decisions.choice: the woman's word, set against Jesus's own word (4:41)
decisions.reason: John contrasts the word of the woman with the word of Jesus himself, which leads many more to believe (4:41-42). Her testimony brings them to him; his word makes their belief their own.

decisions.choice: Samaritans, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Samaritans who believed were men and women, and the word "Samaritans" already includes both, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: word
decisions.reason: Keeps the repeated word that sets her word against his (meaning decision m3); Readable says "what the woman said" and "what Jesus said" to keep the same contrast.

decisions.choice: la palabra de la mujer (L, B); lo que les dijo la mujer (R)
decisions.reason: Keeps the contrast with Jesus's own word in verse 41 (meaning decision m3); Readable says "lo que ... dijo" in both places.

source.text: ὡς οὖν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Σαμαρῖται, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν μεῖναι παρ’ αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ δύο ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore came to him the Samaritans, they were asking him to stay with them; and he stayed there two days.

en.L: So when the Samaritans came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to stay with them; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed there two days.
en.B: When the Samaritans reached {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they kept asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to stay with them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed there for two days.
en.R: The Samaritans came to Jesus and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again and again to stay with them. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed there for two days.

es.L: Así que, cuando los samaritanos vinieron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, le rogaban que se quedara con ellos; y se quedó allí dos días.
es.B: Cuando los samaritanos llegaron adonde estaba, le insistieron en que se quedara con ellos, y se quedó allí dos días.
es.R: Los samaritanos fueron a ver a Jesús y le pidieron una y otra vez que se quedara con ellos. Así que se quedó allí dos días.

sw.L: Basi Wasamaria walipofika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, walikuwa wakimwomba akae pamoja nao; naye akakaa huko siku mbili.
sw.B: Wasamaria walipomfikia, waliendelea kumwomba akae nao, naye akakaa huko kwa siku mbili.
sw.R: Wasamaria walimjia Yesu, wakamwomba tena na tena akae nao. Basi akakaa huko kwa siku mbili.

decisions.choice: a Jew staying as a guest of Samaritans
decisions.reason: Jews and Samaritans did not usually share things (4:9). Here Samaritans invite a Jewish teacher into their homes, and he accepts, eating and lodging with them.

decisions.choice: stay: lodge with them, with the deeper sense of remaining
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary one for staying as a guest, as at 1:38-39, and here it is meant plainly. It is the same verb Jesus later uses for remaining in him (15:4-10).

decisions.choice: stay, stayed
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: the natural word in its ordinary sense.

decisions.choice: kept asking (B); asked again and again (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the repeated request of the imperfect verb.

decisions.choice: quedarse
decisions.reason: The ordinary word for staying as a guest, the same as at 1:38-39 (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ πολλῷ πλείους ἐπίστευσαν διὰ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ, τῇ τε γυναικὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὐκέτι διὰ τὴν σὴν λαλιὰν πιστεύομεν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκηκόαμεν, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: And by much more believed because of the word of him, \v 42 and to the woman they were saying that, "No longer because of your speech do we believe; for ourselves we have heard, and we know that this one is truly the Savior of the world."

en.L: And many more believed because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, \v 42 and they were saying to the woman, "No longer because of your talk do we believe, for we ourselves have heard, and we know that this [one] is truly the Savior of the world."
en.B: Because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own word many more came to believe. \v 42 They said to the woman, "It is no longer your report that makes us believe. We have listened to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} ourselves, and we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is indeed the Savior of the world."
en.R: Many more people believed because of what Jesus said. \v 42 They told the woman, "At first we believed because of what you told us. But now we believe because we have heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for ourselves. We know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} really is the Savior of the world, the one who saves people everywhere."

es.L: Y muchos más creyeron por su palabra, \v 42 y decían a la mujer: «Ya no creemos por lo que tú dijiste, porque nosotros mismos hemos oído, y sabemos que este es verdaderamente el Salvador del mundo».
es.B: Y por su propia palabra muchos más llegaron a creer. \v 42 Le decían a la mujer: «Ya no creemos por lo que tú nos contaste. Nosotros mismos lo hemos escuchado, y sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es de verdad el Salvador del mundo».
es.R: Muchos más creyeron por lo que Jesús decía. \v 42 Le dijeron a la mujer: «Al principio creímos por lo que tú nos contaste. Pero ahora creemos porque nosotros mismos lo hemos oído. Sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es de verdad el Salvador del mundo, el que salva a la gente de todas partes».

sw.L: Na watu wengi zaidi sana waliamini kwa sababu ya neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, \v 42 wakawa wanamwambia yule mwanamke, "Hatuamini tena kwa sababu ya habari uliyotupa, kwa maana sisi wenyewe tumesikia, nasi tunajua kwamba huyu kwa kweli ni Mwokozi wa ulimwengu."
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} mwenyewe watu wengi zaidi wakaamini. \v 42 Wakamwambia yule mwanamke, "Sasa hatuamini kwa sababu ya habari yako. Tumemsikiliza sisi wenyewe, nasi tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakika ni Mwokozi wa ulimwengu."
sw.R: Watu wengi zaidi waliamini kwa sababu ya yale aliyosema Yesu. \v 42 Wakamwambia yule mwanamke, "Mwanzoni tuliamini kwa sababu ya yale uliyotuambia. Lakini sasa tunaamini kwa sababu tumemsikia sisi wenyewe. Tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kweli ni Mwokozi wa ulimwengu, yule anayeokoa watu wa kila mahali."

decisions.choice: many more: a much larger number
decisions.reason: The phrase is "more by much", a comparison of number: many more Samaritans came to believe than the first group.

decisions.choice: your talk: what she had told them
decisions.reason: λαλιὰν means speech or what someone says, and it can mean mere talk. Set beside the "word" of Jesus it is the lesser thing, but they are not scorning her: her report brought them to him (4:39). Now they believe on firsthand hearing.

decisions.choice: they have heard for themselves and know
decisions.reason: Their belief no longer rests on another's report but on Jesus's own word. Both verbs are perfects: what they have heard and know stays with them.

decisions.choice: the Savior: a title for God himself, here given to Jesus
alternatives: a deliverer in a general sense
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament God is Israel's Savior (Isaiah 43:3, 11; 45:15, 21). In the Roman world rulers, the emperors among them, were also hailed as saviors. Only here in John's Gospel is Jesus called Savior; 1 John 4:14 says, "the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world".

decisions.choice: the world: humanity as a whole, Samaritans as well as Jews
decisions.reason: Key term. Here κόσμου means all people. Jesus told the woman that salvation is from the Jews (4:22); Samaritans now confess that it is for the whole world (compare 1:29; 3:16-17).

decisions.choice: the Savior of the world (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the Christ, the Savior of the world (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "the Christ" before "the Savior", as the King James Version reflects. The older manuscripts do not have it. A footnote gives it; a reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: At first we believed because of what you told us. But now
alternatives: We no longer believe because of your words
decisions.reason: "No longer" implies that they had first believed on her word; Readable says so in two plain sentences.

decisions.choice: the one who saves people everywhere
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the title and adds what it means here (meaning decisions m4 and m5).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: "This one" is Jesus; Balanced and Readable use the pronoun with the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Al principio creímos ... Pero ahora
decisions.reason: As in English: "ya no" implies that they had first believed on her word; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: el que salva a la gente de todas partes
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable keeps the title and adds what it means here (meaning decisions m4 and m5).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
decisions.reason: "This one" is Jesus; Balanced and Readable use the stressed pronoun with the setting.

source.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς δύο ἡμέρας ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν·

records.literal_gloss: After now the two days he went out from there into the Galilee;

en.L: And after the two days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out from there into Galilee.
en.B: After the two days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left there for Galilee.
en.R: After those two days, Jesus left that place and went on to Galilee.

es.L: Y después de los dos días salió de allí hacia Galilea.
es.B: Pasados los dos días, salió de allí hacia Galilea.
es.R: Después de esos dos días, Jesús salió de allí y siguió su camino hacia Galilea.

sw.L: Na baada ya zile siku mbili akatoka huko kwenda Galilaya.
sw.B: Baada ya siku hizo mbili aliondoka huko kwenda Galilaya.
sw.R: Baada ya siku hizo mbili, Yesu aliondoka mahali pale, akaendelea na safari kwenda Galilaya.

decisions.choice: the journey of 4:3 resumes
decisions.reason: Jesus had left Judea for Galilee and passed through Samaria on the way (4:3-4). After two days with the Samaritans he goes on.

decisions.choice: he went out from there (SBLGNT)
alternatives: he went out from there and went away (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and went away". The sense is the same, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus at the start of a new scene.

source.text: αὐτὸς γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐμαρτύρησεν ὅτι προφήτης ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ πατρίδι τιμὴν οὐκ ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: Himself for Jesus testified that a prophet in the own homeland honor not has.

en.L: For Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} testified that a prophet in his own homeland has no honor.
en.B: Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} had declared that a prophet is not honored in his own homeland.
en.R: Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} had said that people do not honor a prophet in his own home country.

es.L: Porque Jesús mismo dio testimonio de que un profeta no tiene honra en su propia tierra.
es.B: Jesús mismo había declarado que a un profeta no se le honra en su propia tierra.
es.R: Jesús mismo había dicho que la gente no honra a un profeta en su propia tierra.

sw.L: Kwa maana Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alikuwa ameshuhudia kwamba nabii katika nchi ya kwao hana heshima.
sw.B: Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alikuwa amesema wazi kwamba nabii haheshimiwi katika nchi ya kwao.
sw.R: Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alikuwa amesema kwamba watu hawamheshimu nabii katika nchi ya kwao.

decisions.choice: his own homeland: left open, as the text leaves it
alternatives: Galilee, his home region (Nazareth): he goes there knowing he will not be truly honored
Judea and Jerusalem: he leaves because he was not honored there
decisions.reason: Matthew 13:57, Mark 6:4 and Luke 4:24 use the saying of Nazareth in Galilee, and John calls Jesus a Galilean (1:46; 7:41, 52). But verse 45 says the Galileans welcomed him, which is hard to fit with a saying meant to explain why he went there. On one view his homeland is Galilee, and their welcome is not real honor, since it rests on the signs they saw (2:23-25; 4:48). On another it is Judea, with Jerusalem, the city of David from whose line the Messiah came (7:42); he "came to his own, and his own did not receive him" (1:11), so he left it. The evidence is balanced, and every level keeps "his own homeland" without naming it.

decisions.choice: Jesus himself had said it: a comment by the narrator
decisions.reason: "For" introduces John's explanation of the journey. "Himself" stresses that the saying was Jesus's own. The past tense looks back to something Jesus had said, not to a word spoken at this point.

decisions.choice: homeland: the land or town of one's family
decisions.reason: The word can mean a home town or a native country, which is why the question in m1 arises.

decisions.choice: had declared (B); had said (R)
decisions.reason: Shows that John is recalling a saying (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: his own homeland, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The proverb pictures a prophet like those of Israel, and here it is applied to Jesus; it is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: su propia tierra
decisions.reason: "Su tierra" can mean a home town or a native country, as the Greek word can, so it leaves the question of meaning decision m1 open.

source.text: ὅτε οὖν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐδέξαντο αὐτὸν οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι, πάντα ἑωρακότες ὅσα ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, καὶ αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore he came into the Galilee, received him the Galileans, all things having seen as many as he did in Jerusalem at the feast, also themselves for came to the feast.

en.L: So when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came into Galilee, the Galileans received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having seen all the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did in Jerusalem at the feast; for they themselves also had gone to the feast.
en.B: So when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They had seen all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done in Jerusalem at the festival, since they too had been there for it.
en.R: When Jesus arrived in Galilee, the people there welcomed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They had gone to the Passover festival in Jerusalem too, and they had seen all the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did there.

es.L: Así que, cuando llegó a Galilea, los galileos lo recibieron, habiendo visto todo lo que hizo en Jerusalén durante la fiesta; porque también ellos habían ido a la fiesta.
es.B: Por eso, cuando llegó a Galilea, los galileos lo recibieron bien. Habían visto todo lo que había hecho en Jerusalén durante la fiesta, porque ellos también habían estado allí.
es.R: Cuando Jesús llegó a Galilea, la gente de allí lo recibió bien. Ellos también habían ido a Jerusalén para la fiesta de la Pascua, y habían visto todo lo que Jesús hizo allí.

sw.L: Basi alipofika Galilaya, Wagalilaya walimpokea, wakiwa wameyaona mambo yote aliyoyafanya Yerusalemu wakati wa sikukuu; kwa maana wao pia walikuwa wamekwenda kwenye sikukuu.
sw.B: Basi alipofika Galilaya, Wagalilaya walimkaribisha. Walikuwa wameona yote aliyofanya Yerusalemu wakati wa sikukuu, kwa kuwa wao pia walikuwa wamehudhuria sikukuu hiyo.
sw.R: Yesu alipofika Galilaya, watu wa huko walimkaribisha. Wao pia walikuwa wamekwenda Yerusalemu kwa sikukuu ya Pasaka, nao walikuwa wameona mambo yote aliyoyafanya huko.

decisions.choice: the feast: the Passover of 2:13-23
decisions.reason: Galilean pilgrims went up to Jerusalem for the festivals (Luke 2:41-44). At that Passover Jesus cleared the temple courts and did signs that led many to believe (2:23).

decisions.choice: a welcome based on what they had seen
alternatives: a welcome that shows full faith
decisions.reason: Their welcome rests on the signs they saw. John has already said that Jesus did not entrust himself to belief of that kind (2:23-25), and his words in verse 48 point the same way. This bears on the saying in verse 44.

decisions.choice: the Passover festival
decisions.reason: Readable names the feast meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the journey first, then what they saw
alternatives: having seen ..., for they too had gone
decisions.reason: Readable puts the events in the order they happened.

decisions.choice: la fiesta de la Pascua
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the feast meant (meaning decision m1).

source.text: Ἦλθεν οὖν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὅπου ἐποίησεν τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον.

records.literal_gloss: He came therefore again to the Cana of the Galilee, where he made the water wine.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came again to Cana of Galilee, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made the water [into] wine.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Cana in Galilee, the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had changed the water into wine.
en.R: Jesus went back to Cana in Galilee. This was the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had changed water into wine.

es.L: Vino, pues, otra vez a Caná de Galilea, donde hizo del agua vino.
es.B: Volvió, pues, a Caná de Galilea, donde había convertido el agua en vino.
es.R: Jesús volvió a Caná de Galilea. Era el pueblo donde había convertido el agua en vino.

sw.L: Basi akaja tena Kana ya Galilaya, mahali alipoyafanya maji [kuwa] divai.
sw.B: Basi alirudi Kana ya Galilaya, mahali alipoyageuza maji kuwa divai.
sw.R: Yesu alirudi Kana ya Galilaya. Huo ndio mji ambapo aliyageuza maji kuwa divai.

decisions.choice: a reminder of the first sign at Cana (2:1-11)
decisions.reason: John points back to the first sign so that readers connect the two. The second sign also happens from Cana (4:54), and the two stories have much in common: a request, an answer that seems to hold back, trust in Jesus's word, and belief as the result (2:5, 11; 4:50, 53).

decisions.choice: had changed ... into
decisions.reason: Natural wording for the event of 2:9.

source.text: καὶ ἦν τις βασιλικὸς οὗ ὁ υἱὸς ἠσθένει ἐν Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: And there was a certain royal official whose the son was sick in Capernaum.

en.L: And there was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.
en.B: There was a royal official whose son lay ill at Capernaum.
en.R: In the town of Capernaum there was an official of the king who ruled Galilee. His son was sick.

es.L: Y había cierto funcionario real cuyo hijo estaba enfermo en Capernaúm.
es.B: Había un funcionario real cuyo hijo estaba enfermo en Capernaúm.
es.R: En el pueblo de Capernaúm había un funcionario del rey que gobernaba Galilea. Su hijo estaba enfermo.

sw.L: Na palikuwa na afisa mmoja wa mfalme ambaye mwanawe alikuwa mgonjwa huko Kapernaumu.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na afisa mmoja wa mfalme ambaye mwanawe alikuwa mgonjwa huko Kapernaumu.
sw.R: Katika mji wa Kapernaumu kulikuwa na afisa wa mfalme aliyetawala Galilaya. Mwanawe alikuwa mgonjwa.

decisions.choice: a royal official: most likely an officer of Herod Antipas
alternatives: a member of the royal family
decisions.reason: βασιλικὸς means someone belonging to the king, in his service. In Galilee the ruler was Herod Antipas (4 BC to AD 39); his title was tetrarch, but people called him king (Mark 6:14). The official could have been Jewish or Gentile; John does not say. Matthew 8:5-13 and Luke 7:1-10 tell of a centurion at Capernaum whose servant Jesus healed from a distance; John's account differs in its details, and whether it is the same event is not settled.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a town on the Sea of Galilee, a long walk from Cana
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on the north shore of the lake, far below Cana in the hills (compare 2:12), about 15 to 20 miles away; the exact site of Cana is not certain. Jesus's word reaches the boy without his going there.

decisions.choice: an official of the king who ruled Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable says what "royal" means here (meaning decision m1) without naming Herod, which the text does not do.

decisions.choice: the place first, then the son's illness
decisions.reason: Readable sets the scene in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: un funcionario del rey que gobernaba Galilea
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "royal" means here without naming Herod (meaning decision m1).

source.text: οὗτος ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἥκει ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἠρώτα ἵνα καταβῇ καὶ ἰάσηται αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱόν, ἤμελλεν γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκειν.

records.literal_gloss: This one, having heard that Jesus has come out of the Judea into the Galilee, went away to him and was asking that he would come down and heal his the son, he was about for to die.

en.L: This [man], having heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, went away to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and was asking that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
en.B: Hearing that Jesus had arrived in Galilee from Judea, he went to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kept pleading with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come down and heal his son, because the boy was dying.
en.R: He heard that Jesus had come back from Judea to Galilee. So he went to Jesus and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come down to Capernaum and make his son well. His son was about to die.

es.L: Este, al oír que Jesús había llegado de Judea a Galilea, fue a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y le rogaba que bajara y sanara a su hijo, porque estaba a punto de morir.
es.B: Al enterarse de que Jesús había llegado de Judea a Galilea, fue a verlo y le suplicaba que bajara a sanar a su hijo, porque el muchacho se estaba muriendo.
es.R: Oyó que Jesús había vuelto de Judea a Galilea. Entonces fue a verlo y le rogó que bajara a Capernaúm a curar a su hijo, porque su hijo estaba a punto de morir.

sw.L: Huyu, aliposikia kwamba Yesu amekuja kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya, alimwendea, akawa anamwomba ashuke na kumponya mwanawe, kwa maana alikuwa karibu kufa.
sw.B: Aliposikia kwamba Yesu amefika Galilaya kutoka Uyahudi, alimwendea, akaendelea kumsihi ashuke amponye mwanawe, kwa sababu kijana alikuwa anakaribia kufa.
sw.R: Alisikia kwamba Yesu amerudi kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya. Basi alikwenda kwa Yesu, akamwomba sana ashuke Kapernaumu amponye mwanawe. Mwanawe alikuwa karibu kufa.

decisions.choice: was asking: kept pleading
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows a request made again and again. The same verb was used of the Samaritans' request in 4:40.

decisions.choice: come down: from the hill country of Cana to the lakeshore
decisions.reason: Capernaum is far lower than Cana, so one goes "down" to it (2:12). The official asks Jesus to come with him; he assumes the healing needs Jesus to be there.

decisions.choice: he was about to die: at the point of death
alternatives: he was going to die someday
decisions.reason: The verb means to be on the verge of something. The boy was dying.

decisions.choice: to Capernaum
decisions.reason: Readable names the place (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the boy
decisions.reason: Shows that the son, not the father, was dying.

decisions.choice: a Capernaúm
decisions.reason: Readable names the place (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: el muchacho
decisions.reason: Shows that the son, not the father, was dying.

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐὰν μὴ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἴδητε, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε.

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jesus to him, "Unless signs and wonders you see, not not you will believe."

en.L: So Jesus said to him, "Unless you [people] see signs and wonders, you will certainly not believe."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "None of you will believe unless you see signs and wonders."
en.R: Jesus said to the man, "You people will not believe unless you see signs and wonders."

es.L: Entonces Jesús le dijo: «Si no {{plural_you:ven|veis}} señales y prodigios, de ningún modo {{plural_you:creerán|creeréis}}».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} creerá si no ve señales y prodigios».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes no creerán si no ven|Vosotros no creeréis si no veis}} señales y prodigios».

sw.L: Basi Yesu akamwambia, "Msipoona ishara na maajabu, hakika hamtaamini."
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "Hakuna hata mmoja wenu atakayeamini msipoona ishara na maajabu."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia yule mtu, "Ninyi watu hamtaamini msipoona ishara na maajabu."

decisions.choice: you: plural, spoken to the man but about the people at large
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the official, but both verbs are plural. His words take in the Galileans who welcomed him because of what they had seen (4:45), and the official with them.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the phrase for the deeds of the exodus
decisions.reason: The pair is used in the Old Testament for what God did in Egypt (Exodus 7:3; Deuteronomy 4:34; 6:22). It appears only here in John. Joined with "wonders", "signs" here means the striking deed itself rather than what it points to.

decisions.choice: a warning against belief that waits for proof
decisions.reason: The double negative (οὐ μὴ) makes the statement strong: without such deeds you will not believe at all. Jesus does not refuse the man; he challenges a belief that depends on seeing (2:23-25; 20:29). The man answers by pleading again, and then believes Jesus's word before he sees anything (4:50).

decisions.choice: [people] (L); None of you (B); You people (R)
decisions.reason: Shows that "you" is plural (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: certainly not
decisions.reason: Literal shows the strong double negative (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: plural verbs; ninguno de ustedes (B)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to one man, but the verbs are plural (meaning decision m1). Spanish shows that in the verb, so Literal needs no "[people]".

decisions.choice: de ningún modo
decisions.reason: Literal shows the strong double negative (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: msipoona, hamtaamini: the plural is in the verb
decisions.reason: Jesus answers one man but speaks of "you" in the plural. Swahili marks the plural in the verbs (m-, ham-), so Literal needs no bracketed "[people]"; Balanced and Readable spell it out, as the English does.

source.text: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ βασιλικός· Κύριε, κατάβηθι πρὶν ἀποθανεῖν τὸ παιδίον μου.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the royal official, "Sir, come down before dies the little child of me."

en.L: The royal official says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Sir, come down before my little child dies."
en.B: The official pleaded, "Sir, come down before my little boy dies."
en.R: The official said, "Sir, please come before my child dies!"

es.L: Le dice el funcionario real: «Señor, baja antes de que muera mi niño».
es.B: El funcionario le suplicó: «Señor, baja antes de que se muera mi niño».
es.R: El funcionario le dijo: «¡Señor, por favor, ven antes de que mi hijo se muera!».

sw.L: Yule afisa wa mfalme anamwambia, "Shuka, bwana, kabla mtoto wangu mdogo hajafa."
sw.B: Yule afisa akamsihi, "Shuka, bwana, kabla kijana wangu mdogo hajafa."
sw.R: Yule afisa akasema, "Tafadhali njoo, bwana, kabla mtoto wangu hajafa!"

decisions.choice: Sir: a respectful address
alternatives: Lord, a confession of who Jesus is
decisions.reason: The address is the polite form used to anyone of standing; the Samaritan woman uses it at 4:11, 15 and 19. The official does not yet know who Jesus is; he believes later (4:53). A footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: my little child: a tender word
decisions.reason: The father uses a diminutive, "little child". John calls the boy his son, and the servants call him "the boy" (4:51).

decisions.choice: he does not give up
decisions.reason: Like Jesus's mother at Cana (2:3-5), the official is not turned away by Jesus's reply; he simply asks again.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: Shows the polite address (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: please
decisions.reason: Readable shows the urgent pleading in the words.

decisions.choice: pleaded
decisions.reason: His words are an urgent plea, which the verb shows.

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: As at 4:11: Spanish "señor" is the polite address and also "Lord" (meaning decision m1). L and B keep "mi niño" for the father's tender word (m2).

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πορεύου· ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Jesus, "Go; the son of you lives."

en.L: Jesus says to him, "Go; your son lives."
en.B: Jesus told him, "Go. Your son lives."
en.R: Jesus told him, "Go home. Your son is alive and well."

es.L: Jesús le dice: «Ve, tu hijo vive».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Vete. Tu hijo vive».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Vuelve a casa. Tu hijo está vivo y sano».

sw.L: Yesu anamwambia, "Nenda; mwanao yu hai."
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda. Mwanao yu hai."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda nyumbani. Mwana wako yu hai na mzima."

decisions.choice: lives: will not die, is well again
alternatives: will live (a promise about the future)
decisions.reason: The verb is present: the boy lives now. In Hebrew usage, to "live" after an illness is to recover (2 Kings 1:2; 8:8-10). Verse 53 shows that the healing happened at the moment Jesus spoke.

decisions.choice: possibly an echo of Elijah: "See, your son lives" (1 Kings 17:23)
alternatives: no echo; the words are ordinary
decisions.reason: Elijah gave a widow back her son with almost the same words in the Greek Old Testament. The phrase is ordinary enough to occur without any echo, so the link is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Go: Jesus sends him home without coming
decisions.reason: The official asked Jesus to come down. Jesus does not go; he speaks the word and sends the father on his way.

decisions.choice: is alive and well
decisions.reason: Readable says what "lives" means here (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "lives", which carries the echo (m2) and returns in verses 51 and 53.

decisions.choice: home
decisions.reason: Readable says where he is to go.

decisions.choice: está vivo y sano (R); vive (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "lives" means here (meaning decision m1); Literal and Balanced keep "vive", which carries the possible echo (m2) and returns in verses 51 and 53.

source.text: ἐπίστευσεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐπορεύετο.

records.literal_gloss: Believed the man the word that said to him the Jesus and was going.

en.L: The man believed the word which Jesus said to him, and set out.
en.B: The man believed what Jesus had said to him and started for home.
en.R: The man believed what Jesus told him, and he started back home.

es.L: El hombre creyó la palabra que Jesús le dijo, y se fue.
es.B: El hombre creyó lo que Jesús le había dicho y emprendió el regreso a casa.
es.R: El hombre creyó lo que Jesús le dijo, y se puso en camino a su casa.

sw.L: Yule mtu aliliamini neno ambalo Yesu alimwambia, akaenda zake.
sw.B: Yule mtu aliamini yale Yesu aliyomwambia, akaanza safari ya kurudi nyumbani.
sw.R: Yule mtu aliamini kile Yesu alichomwambia, akaanza kurudi nyumbani.

decisions.choice: he believed Jesus's word before seeing anything
decisions.reason: "Believe" with the word as its object means accepting that what Jesus said is true. Jesus had said that people believe only when they see (4:48); this man believes the word alone. When the word proves true, he believes in the fuller sense (4:53).

decisions.choice: was going: was on his way
decisions.reason: The imperfect leaves him on the road, where the servants meet him (4:51).

decisions.choice: started for home / started back home
decisions.reason: Says where he went; Literal "set out" keeps the bare verb.

decisions.choice: creyó la palabra / lo que
decisions.reason: With the word as its object the verb means accepting that it is true (meaning decision m1), so Spanish says "creer" + object, as in 2:22, not "creer en".

source.text: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι ὁ παῖς αὐτοῦ ζῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Already now he going down, the slaves of him met him, saying that the boy of him lives.

en.L: And while he was already going down, his slaves met him, saying that his boy lives.
en.B: While he was still on the way down, his slaves met him with the news that his boy was alive.
en.R: While he was still on his way home, his slaves came to meet him. They told him, "Your son is alive and well!"

es.L: Y cuando ya bajaba, sus esclavos le salieron al encuentro, diciendo que su muchacho vivía.
es.B: Cuando todavía iba bajando, sus esclavos le salieron al encuentro con la noticia de que el muchacho vivía.
es.R: Cuando todavía iba de camino a casa, sus esclavos salieron a encontrarlo. Le dijeron: «¡Tu hijo está vivo y sano!».

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akishuka, watumwa wake walikutana naye, wakisema kwamba mtoto wake yu hai.
sw.B: Alipokuwa bado njiani akishuka, watumwa wake walikutana naye na habari kwamba mtoto wake yu hai.
sw.R: Alipokuwa bado njiani kurudi nyumbani, watumwa wake walikuja kumlaki. Wakamwambia, "Mwana wako yu hai na mzima!"

decisions.choice: household slaves, owned by the official
decisions.reason: δοῦλοι were slaves belonging to the household, not hired staff. A royal official would have had several. They come out to give the news.

decisions.choice: his boy: the official's son
decisions.reason: The word can mean a boy or a servant; here it is the son of verse 46, as "his son" in verse 53 shows.

decisions.choice: lives: the word Jesus used
decisions.reason: The servants' news repeats Jesus's word "lives" (4:50), and verse 53 repeats it again. John uses the repetition to show that the word came true.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: The same word is "slave" everywhere in this translation (Philippians 1:1; 2:7). "Servants" would hide that they were owned by the household; meaning decision m1 says what their position was.

decisions.choice: direct speech: "Your son is alive and well!"
decisions.reason: Readable gives their words as they spoke them, which is easier to follow, and uses the same words as verse 50.

decisions.choice: esclavos
decisions.reason: As in English: the same word is "esclavo" everywhere in this translation; "criados" would hide that they were owned by the household (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: watumwa
decisions.reason: These are slaves owned by the official, as the meaning note says. "Mtumwa" is a slave; "mtumishi" is a servant who works for pay, which would soften what they were. As the English has "slaves".

source.text: ἐπύθετο οὖν τὴν ὥραν παρ’ αὐτῶν ἐν ᾗ κομψότερον ἔσχεν· εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐχθὲς ὥραν ἑβδόμην ἀφῆκεν αὐτὸν ὁ πυρετός.

records.literal_gloss: He inquired therefore the hour from them in which better he had; they said therefore to him that, "Yesterday [at the] hour seventh left him the fever."

en.L: So he asked them the hour in which he had gotten better; so they said to him, "Yesterday at [the] seventh hour the fever left him."
en.B: So he asked them at what time the boy had begun to recover, and they told him, "The fever left him yesterday at about one in the afternoon."
en.R: He asked them when his son had started to get better. They said, "Yesterday, at about one o'clock in the afternoon, the fever went away."

es.L: Les preguntó, pues, la hora en que había empezado a mejorar; y le dijeron: «Ayer a la hora séptima lo dejó la fiebre».
es.B: Entonces les preguntó a qué hora había empezado el muchacho a mejorar, y le dijeron: «Ayer, como a la una de la tarde, se le quitó la fiebre».
es.R: Les preguntó cuándo había empezado a mejorar su hijo. Le dijeron: «Ayer, como a la una de la tarde, se le fue la fiebre».

sw.L: Basi akawauliza saa ambayo alianza kupata nafuu; wakamwambia, "Jana saa saba homa ilimwacha."
sw.B: Basi akawauliza ni saa ngapi mtoto alianza kupata nafuu, nao wakamwambia, "Homa ilimwacha jana yapata saa saba mchana."
sw.R: Akawauliza mwanawe alianza kupata nafuu lini. Wakasema, "Jana, kama saa saba mchana, homa iliondoka."

decisions.choice: he had begun to get better
decisions.reason: The phrase means to be better, to be on the mend. The father asks when the improvement began; the servants answer that the fever left him altogether.

decisions.choice: the seventh hour: about one in the afternoon
alternatives: about seven in the morning, counting from midnight
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, so the seventh hour was about one in the afternoon (see 1:39; 11:9). Some have argued that John counts from midnight, which would make it seven in the morning. A footnote gives the literal wording and the other way of counting.

decisions.choice: yesterday: the father reached home the next day
decisions.reason: The journey down to Capernaum was long, so the father met his servants the following day. A Jewish day began at sunset, so if they met after nightfall, the afternoon before was already "yesterday" even if he had traveled only a few hours.

decisions.choice: about one in the afternoon
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the clock time, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the boy (B); his son (R)
decisions.reason: Shows who got better.

decisions.choice: como a la una de la tarde
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the clock time, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: saa saba at every level; mchana added at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The seventh hour from sunrise is "saa saba" in Swahili time, about one in the afternoon, so the literal words are also the modern time, as in 1:39 and 4:6.

source.text: ἔγνω οὖν ὁ πατὴρ ὅτι ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐν ᾗ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ, καὶ ἐπίστευσεν αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ οἰκία αὐτοῦ ὅλη.

records.literal_gloss: Knew therefore the father that [it was] in that the hour in which said to him the Jesus, "The son of you lives," and believed he himself and the household of him whole.

en.L: So the father knew that [it was] at that hour in which Jesus said to him, "Your son lives," and he himself believed, and his whole household.
en.B: Then the father realized that it had happened at the very hour Jesus had said to him, "Your son lives." So he came to believe, together with all his household.
en.R: Then the father realized that this was the exact time when Jesus had said to him, "Your son is alive and well." So he and everyone in his home believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Conoció entonces el padre que [fue] a aquella hora en que Jesús le dijo: «Tu hijo vive»; y creyó él y toda su casa.
es.B: El padre se dio cuenta de que había sido a la misma hora en que Jesús le había dicho: «Tu hijo vive». Y creyeron él y todos los de su casa.
es.R: Entonces el padre se dio cuenta de que fue justo a la hora en que Jesús le había dicho: «Tu hijo está vivo y sano». Así que él y todos los de su casa creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Basi baba yake akajua kwamba [ilikuwa] saa ile ile ambayo Yesu alimwambia, "Mwanao yu hai," naye mwenyewe akaamini, pamoja na nyumba yake yote.
sw.B: Ndipo baba yake alipotambua kwamba ilitokea saa ile ile ambayo Yesu alikuwa amemwambia, "Mwanao yu hai." Basi akaamini, yeye pamoja na watu wote wa nyumbani mwake.
sw.R: Ndipo baba yake alipotambua kwamba huo ndio wakati hasa ambao Yesu alimwambia, "Mwana wako yu hai na mzima." Basi yeye na kila mtu wa nyumbani mwake walimwamini Yesu.

decisions.choice: he believed: he became a believer in Jesus
alternatives: he believed the word again, as in verse 50
decisions.reason: In verse 50 he believed what Jesus said. Here the verb stands without an object, as in 1:50 and 20:29: he now believes in Jesus himself. The story moves from asking for a sign, to trusting the word, to belief.

decisions.choice: his whole household: family and servants
decisions.reason: A household included the family and its slaves and dependents. In Acts whole households come to believe together (Acts 10:2, 44; 16:15, 31-34; 18:8).

decisions.choice: the father: the official is now named by his relation to the boy
decisions.reason: John calls him a royal official (4:46, 49), then the man (4:50), and now the father. The title gives way to the parent whose son lives.

decisions.choice: in him
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they believed in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: is alive and well
decisions.reason: As in verse 50.

decisions.choice: todos los de su casa
decisions.reason: A household included family, slaves and dependents (meaning decision m2); "familia" would leave the slaves out.

decisions.choice: en él
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says whom they believed in (meaning decision m1).

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ πάλιν δεύτερον σημεῖον ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλθὼν ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.

records.literal_gloss: This now again second sign did the Jesus having come out of the Judea into the Galilee.

en.L: And this again [was the] second sign [that] Jesus did, having come from Judea into Galilee.
en.B: Jesus did this, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} second sign, after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come back from Judea to Galilee.
en.R: This was the second sign Jesus did. It happened after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to Galilee from Judea.

es.L: Y esta, de nuevo, [fue la] segunda señal [que] hizo Jesús, al venir de Judea a Galilea.
es.B: Esta fue la segunda señal que hizo Jesús, después de volver de Judea a Galilea.
es.R: Esta fue la segunda señal que hizo Jesús. Sucedió después de que volvió de Judea a Galilea.

sw.L: Na hii tena [ilikuwa] ishara ya pili [ambayo] Yesu aliifanya, akiwa amekuja kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya.
sw.B: Yesu alifanya ishara hii, ishara {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya pili, baada ya kurudi kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya.
sw.R: Hii ilikuwa ishara ya pili aliyoifanya Yesu. Ilitokea baada ya kurudi Galilaya kutoka Uyahudi.

decisions.choice: again a second sign: the second sign, counted from 2:11
alternatives: a second sign done on a second journey from Judea
decisions.reason: "Again" and "second" together stress the count. The first sign was at Cana (2:11); John mentions other signs in Jerusalem (2:23) but does not number them. The count marks the two signs at Cana, which frame the story from 2:1 to 4:54.

decisions.choice: sign: a deed that points to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: Key term in John (2:11). Here the sign shows that Jesus's word gives life, from a distance and at once (compare 5:24-25).

decisions.choice: "again" not repeated
alternatives: this again was the second sign
decisions.reason: "Again" with "second" says the same thing twice (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: "de nuevo" not repeated
decisions.reason: As in English: "again" with "second" says the same thing twice (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps it.
